overlays.hook: King had the dream. *He built the march.*

beats.text: In 1947, he rode buses through the South to challenge segregation, and was sentenced to a chain gang.
In Montgomery, he became a close adviser to a young Martin Luther King Jr.
But Rustin was gay, and some leaders feared it would be used against the movement.
In 1963, he had less than two months to organize the March on Washington.

visual.title: Two months
visual.sub: to organize the March on Washington

beats.text: On August 28, more than 250,000 people came. It was one of the largest demonstrations the country had ever seen.

visual.caption: Martin Luther King Jr. at the March on Washington, August 28, 1963

beats.text: Days before, Senator Strom Thurmond attacked him on the Senate floor, calling him a communist, a draft dodger and a homosexual.
His title was only deputy director, and for years his name stayed in the background.
In 2013, fifty years later, he was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
And in 2020, California pardoned him for his 1953 conviction.
King had the dream. Bayard Rustin built the march.

facts.claim: Rustin was the main organizer of the 1963 March on Washington.
1947 Journey of Reconciliation; arrested in North Carolina, chain gang.
Advised King during the Montgomery bus boycott.
1953 Pasadena arrest; pushed aside because he was gay.
Less than two months to organize the march.
Thurmond attacked him on the Senate floor (communist, draft dodger, homosexual).
Title: deputy director of the march.
Posthumous Presidential Medal of Freedom, 20 Nov 2013, President Obama.
California Gov. Newsom pardoned him in 2020.
